Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLO (p95/p99) end-to-end latency — hosted API vs current provider

Hi Sarah / Raj — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before a technical deep-dive: 

Summary of your requirements (as discussed):
- E2E latency targets (client -> API -> model -> client) for typical user flows: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms for single-turn prompts at ~512 tokens.
- Sustained throughput baseline: ~100-150 RPS.
- Peak concurrency: 200 concurrent requests (bursts up to 500 for short windows).
- Streaming behavior: server-sent token streaming (chunked HTTP) with per-token latency expectations (first-token <= 150ms ideally, steady-state token emission <= 50-80ms).
- Reliability: graceful degradation / fallback to smaller model should p99 tiers spike.

What we (Redwood) committed to check internally / provide:
1) Baseline hosted API latency profiles for comparable model sizes (end-to-end p95/p99 numbers including network & tokenization overhead).
2) Typical throughput/concurrency characteristics and recommended concurrency controls (max tokens-in-flight, batching windows).
3) Clarify streaming implementation details and what metrics we telemetry for per-token latency.
4) Propose a short PoC: 24-72 hour test using a sample workload (you provide representative prompts / traffic shape) where we run against both our hosted API and your current provider to capture comparable telemetry.

Action items / next steps:
- Sarah: please share an anonymized sample of recent request traces (p95/p99 CSV or equivalent) and one short call recording if helpful - we can ingest and baseline against that.
- Redwood (Marissa/Aditya/Laura): we'll provide a short tech deck + expected hosted API p95/p99 numbers and a PoC plan by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule tech deep-dive: propose next Wed 10am PT.

Attachments: none in this note - please send your CSVs/exports when ready.

Thanks - Laura

Hi all - quick internal + public-facing clarification from the engineering side: 

Short answers to Sarah's questions:
1) Hosted API typical end-to-end (public internet included) for comparable model sizes and 512-token payloads: p95 ≈ 180-230ms, p99 ≈ 400-520ms. These figures assume reasonable client-to-region connectivity (US-west client -> US-west region). We can provide region-specific measurements for your east-coast users too, which will add ~20-40ms typical network RTT.

2) Streaming & backpressure: our runtime supports chunked streaming (HTTP SSE / chunked transfer). For tail-latency mitigation we use:
  - Adaptive continuous batching that keeps batch windows short under low latency SLOs.
  - Priority routing and warm pools for bursty customers (pre-warmed workers tied to the reserved capacity).
  - Token emission starts as soon as first token is available - first-token latency is typically <150ms on warm workers.
  - When concurrency spikes, we apply smart queuing + autoscaling; if autoscaling can't keep up, we recommend a client-side concurrency cap (we suggest 200 concurrent requests for FinLytics baseline, with token-level timeouts at ~10s).

3) Throughput: we have customers running sustained 100-500 RPS across pooled capacity. For the PoC we'll recommend a small reserved pool to eliminate cold-start variance.

Proposed PoC (24-72 hour):
- You provide representative prompts and (optionally) a traffic replay (anonymized).
- Redwood will run two parallel runs: (A) your current provider (using the same request set) and (B) Redwood hosted API in your preferred region.
- We'll collect end-to-end p50/p95/p99, first-token latency, per-token emission rate, and resource metrics.
- Deliverable: side-by-side report + recommendations (batching, concurrency caps, cached prefixes) and a short runbook for production rollout.

I'll draft a short tech deck + PoC runbook and share by EOD today. Laura - can you lock down the deep-dive slot (Wed 10am PT) with Sarah?

Thanks - Marissa
